atoms.text: Michael is an electrician and is building a new circuit for the lightbulb in his kitchen.

atoms.a: What component could he add to the circuit to save electricity?
Why would adding a switch help to save electricity?
b: ++The bulb could be turned on and off as needed.
The bulb wouldn’t use any electricity.
The bulb would always be turned on.

atoms.text: Now Michael is working on a toy fire engine for his nephew. The toy has a light that spins, but his nephew doesn’t want it to spin anymore.

atoms.a: What could Michael change to stop the light from spinning?
b: ++He could take the motor out of the circuit.
He could add another cell to the circuit.
He could take the bulb out of the circuit.

atoms.a: What additional side effect would this have on the circuit?
b: ++The bulb would get more power and shine more brightly.
The bulb would get less power and shine more dimmly
The bulb would get more power and start spinning.

atoms.text: Lastly, Michael tries to fix his niece’s alarm clock. The alarm is so quiet that it doesn’t wake her up. When Michael opens the clock up, he finds this circuit.

b: The cell isn’t connected to the buzzer.

atoms.a: Why would swapping the long wire for a shorter one make the alarm louder?

++Less energy would be wasted by the electricity having to travel so far.
The cell would become more powerful.
